tagline: Up eastern Kentucky, with the singers named at every county line.
intro: US 23 comes in from Virginia near Jenkins and runs north the length of eastern Kentucky on four lanes, along the Levisa Fork past Pikeville, Prestonsburg and Paintsville, then beside the Big Sandy River to Catlettsburg and Ashland and along the Ohio to Greenup.

A 1994 act of the General Assembly named it the Country Music Highway, and at each county line a sign lists the stars from that county. The Big Sandy Valley alone claims Loretta Lynn and Crystal Gayle, Naomi and Wynonna Judd, Billy Ray Cyrus, Tom T. Hall, Ricky Skaggs, Keith Whitley, Dwight Yoakam and Patty Loveless. The signs need the room.

moments.title: Pikeville Cut-Through
moments.text: Fourteen years of work through Peach Orchard Mountain made a cut 523 feet deep, and the highway, the railroad and the Levisa Fork now all go through it together.

moments.title: Paintsville
moments.text: Crystal Gayle was born here in 1951, and the U.S. 23 Country Music Highway Museum profiles her, her sister Loretta Lynn, Hylo Brown and others who grew up near the road.

moments.title: Butcher Hollow
moments.text: Loretta Lynn was born here, in a cabin on a hill in Butcher Holler as the song has it, while her daddy worked the Van Lear coal mines.
